`z.record` now drops any entry whose key schema outputs `"__proto__"`. It raises no issue and writes no value, and the result keeps `Object.prototype` as its prototype. The new test and the rest of `record.test.ts` pass, along with the type check. I didn't run the full suite or the lint step.

The fix is in `packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts`, in the general record branch. After the key schema runs and passes, a key equal to `"__proto__"` is skipped before the value schema runs. The check sits on the output key, so it covers every way of changing the key (`.toLowerCase()`, `.trim()`, `.transform(...)` and so on). Both sync and async paths go through the same loop, so `parse`, `parseAsync` and async value schemas are covered. The raw-input `"__proto__"` check is unchanged, and normal normalization still works.

I added one test to `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/record.test.ts`. It covers the async path with `.toLowerCase()` and an async refinement, plus the sync path with `.trim()`. Each case checks that the prototype is `Object.prototype`, that `.a` is undefined, and that the only own key is the normalized one.

I didn't add a mini-API test. The classic and mini record schemas run the same core parser, so the fix applies to both.
